title: The Mississippi River
passages: The Mississippi River begins as a small stream flowing out of Lake Itasca in northern Minnesota. There, the water is so shallow that visitors can walk across it on stepping stones. From that modest start, the river travels about 2,340 miles south, making it one of the longest rivers in North America. Its name comes from the Ojibwe words misi ziibi, which mean "great river." Ojibwe people have lived near its HEADWATERS for centuries, gathering wild rice from the lakes and marshes nearby. According to the National Park Service, a single raindrop falling into Lake Itasca would need about 90 days to reach the end of the river.

Along its journey, the river touches 10 states: Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, Illinois, Missouri, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas, Mississippi and Louisiana. Large TRIBUTARIES such as the Missouri and Ohio Rivers pour into it, and its basin drains water from parts of 31 states and 2 Canadian provinces, more than 40 percent of the lower 48 states. Near its end, the river flows past New Orleans, a city famous for jazz, Creole cooking and Mardi Gras parades. Finally, it carries tons of SEDIMENT into a wide, marshy DELTA and empties into the Gulf of Mexico.
